 This Criminal Petition, Coming On For, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order
The petitioner is before this Court calling in question seeking enlargement of bail for it having been done on by the learned Sessions Judge on SC No.1/2023 in terms of it.
2. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent.

3. Brief facts are as follows:
The second respondent is the complainant father of the victim on 17.09.2022 the victim girl who was missing.

A complaint was came to be registered in Crime No.164/2022 for offences punishable under Section 363 of the IPC present to which the petitioner is taken into custody on 30.01.2022 and remains in custody since then.
After the investigation charge sheet comes to be filed against the petitioner for offences punishable under Sections 363, 344, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
After filing of the charge sheet the petitioner knocks the door of the learned Sessions Judge seeking enlargement of bail, it is turned down in terms of the order as aforesaid.

The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the victim had voluntarily comes with the petitioner and stayed with him for 40 days and therefore entitled to be in the lis enlarged on bail.

4. The learned High Court Government Pleader would however seek dismissal of the petition on the ground that the offences involved are punishable under Sections 363, 344, 376(2)(N) of IPC and Section s 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and therefore bail should not be granted.
5. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the respective learned counsel and perused the material on record.

7. A perusal at the aforesaid statement would clearly indicate the fact that, the victim and the petitioner were in love, the victim herself called the petitioner and asked her to take her to certain places where the victim states that she stayed with him for 40 days and thereafter the crime comes to be registered.

In the light of the said statement and the voluntary act of the victim who was at that time aged 17 years 7 months and the fact that the petitioner has been in custody from 31.10.2022 for over 7 months now.
I deem it appropriate to enlarge the petitioner on grant of regular bail imposing some stringent conditions.

8. For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER
The criminal petition is allowed.

The petitioner shall be released on bail in connection with Sessions Case No.1 of 2023 pending on the file of Additional District and Sessions Judge Gadag (Crime No.164/2022), subject to the following conditions:
(i) The petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees two lakhs only) with one surety for the like sum to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Court.
